title: The principal-open section comparison for the matching ring is bijective.
statement: Let A be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], C its maximal-ideal adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and U an open of Spec A consisting exactly of the points other than the closed point [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let q:Y→U and s:E→Spec C be finite morphisms [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and D:CompletionGluingData A U q E s the supplied overlap identification [def-sbc-punctured-completion-matching-sections]. For f∈A assume D(f)⊆U. Put V=(U→Spec A)⁻¹(D(f)), r=D.modelMap restricted to U, W=r⁻¹(V), and p=D.puncturedMap. Then the ring homomorphism Γ(W,O)→Γ(p⁻¹(W),O) induced by p restricted to W is bijective. The two restricted schemes and their ring map are the actual restrictions of the explicit matching-sections candidate; no new gluing object is chosen.

source.place: Tag 0BLH, proof; Tag 05ER, localized comparison; Tag 05EU, compatibility with algebra structures

proof.text: The containment D(f)⊆U implies f lies in the maximal ideal, since the closed point is excluded. Choose finitely many generators of that ideal and include f. Finiteness of q makes its restriction to each D(g) affine, with algebra B_g; finiteness of s makes E affine, with algebra B′. The supplied overlap identification gives B′ localized at g identified with B_g tensor_A C. Pairwise overlap identifications and their cocycle come from q. These are the gluing data of Tag 05ER.

The sheaf equalizer for the finite principal-open cover of Y identifies Γ(Y) with the compatible B_g sections. Consequently H⁰ of this gluing datum is the explicit ring pullback D.matchingRing. Completion is flat and induces the identity modulo the maximal ideal, so the localized comparison in Tag 05ER applies, giving D.matchingRing localized at f isomorphic to B_f by the first projection. Tag 05EU identifies its multiplication and unit with the componentwise matching-ring structure.

The target restriction W is the inverse image of D(f) in the affine scheme Spec(D.matchingRing), since D(f)⊆U. Its sections are the preceding localization. The identity p followed by r equals q identifies p⁻¹(W) with q⁻¹(V), whose sections are B_f. The Spec–Γ adjunction and the definition of fromPunctured identify the induced appTop map with the localized first projection, hence it is bijective. If D(f) is empty, both rings are zero and this remains true.

theorem puncturedMap_basicOpen_appTop_bijective
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    {U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens}
    (hU : ∀ x : Spec (.of A), x ∈ U ↔ x ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} {q : Y ⟶ U.toScheme} [IsFinite q]
    {E : Scheme.{u}} {s : E ⟶ Spec
      (.of (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A))} [IsFinite s]
    (D : CompletionGluingData A U q E s) (f : A)
    (hf : (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f : (Spec (.of A)).Opens) ≤ U) :
    Function.Bijective
      (D.puncturedMap ∣_ ((D.modelMap ∣_ U) ⁻¹ᵁ
        (U.ι ⁻¹ᵁ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f))).appTop.hom
